generation.explanation: The function y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D has four knobs: A is the amplitude (height of the wave), B controls the frequency (period = 2π/B), C is the phase shift (slides the wave left/right), and D is the vertical shift (moves the midline up/down). The faint gray curve is the reference y = sin(x), the dashed gray line is the midline y = D, and the gold dot marks (C, D) — the point where each cycle begins. Use the sliders to morph the blue wave and watch the equation and stats update live.
